title: MCQ Rewrite Backlog Analysis
methodology: Based on cognitive level distribution across all 5 packs, excluding S061/S062 already-rewritten items and recent S899-S60 authoring (Packs C+D Sections E+F)

rewrite_candidate_inventory.pack_e_dl016_blocked: ~525 items (entire Pack E pending DL-016 resolution)

priority_sections_by_roi.roi_rationale: COSO-based scenarios naturally support Evaluate-level judgment. Many items already have rich multi-paragraph scenarios that only need cognitive elevation.
Budgeting tradeoffs, transfer pricing, and responsibility accounting are inherently decision-oriented. Definition-driven items convert well to scenario-based Evaluate items.
ASC classification judgments (subsequent events, debt classification, revenue recognition) support genuine professional judgment scenarios.
TOC, relevant costing, keep-or-drop, make-or-buy naturally support analysis with specific financial data.
AI/ML risk, ERP controls, data governance — emerging topics benefit from scenario-based testing.
ROI/RI, variance analysis, balanced scorecard — smaller pool but high per-item quality impact.

alternative_paths: Fresh-authored Evaluate items replacing DL-012 clones
Pack E DL-016 repair unlocking ~409 Understand items for rewrite
Case bank item difficulty recalibration (currently 100% Moderate)

maximum_rewrite_capacity.per_wave_applied: ~14 items (Packs A+B only; Pack E blocked, C+D E+F recent authoring)

blockers.impact: Blocks ~525 Pack E items from safe individual rewriting
blockers.resolution: Full Pack E rotation-group repair before content rewrites

blockers.blocker: S899-S60 recent authoring — Packs C+D Sections E+F
blockers.impact: ~100 items recently authored, should not be rewritten until stabilized
blockers.resolution: Allow 2-3 waves of stabilization before targeting these sections

blockers.blocker: DL-012 clone archival — Pack C+D Section E
blockers.impact: 140 clone items taking up QID slots that could hold fresh Evaluate content
blockers.resolution: Archive clones, replace with fresh-authored Evaluate items (S380 model)

recommendation.rationale: The Session 61+62 pilot has demonstrated that substantive rewrites produce higher-value improvements than metadata reclassification, difficulty relabeling, or explanation expansion alone. The methodology is repeatable, produces consistent quality, and directly attacks the cognitive-gap and Evaluate-track objectives.
recommendation.recommended_frequency: One wave per session cycle, targeting 10-14 items per wave
recommendation.next_wave_target: Session 63 — Pack A Section A and Pack B Section A (financial reporting judgment items)
